themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints exploded to 6 THIS WEEK, a 860% spike versus 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score 7.72), signaling potential widespread disease, storm damage, or deferred maintenance affecting neighborhood canopy and public safety.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score 7.72)
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for 'new equipment for maintenance' to Parks & Recreation
510 building permits filed in past 90 days may indicate ongoing construction that could stress trees
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Dept on whether a disease or pest is affecting Williamsbridge's street trees; request inspection data
Canvass residents on whether they've noticed tree deaths in their blocks and photograph affected areas
Investigate whether deferred maintenance funding is responsible for the spike

themes_detail.label: Homeless Assistance Surge
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 300% spike from the 1.0 weekly average (z-score 3.0), indicating either an influx of unhoused individuals or increased resident reporting of encampments and crisis situations.
evidence: 4 homeless person assistance complaints THIS WEEK vs 1.0 weekly average (300% spike, z-score 3.0)
No recent Reddit discussions or local news mentions, suggesting this emerging issue has not yet broken publicly
Timing coincides with winter weather, which typically increases homelessness-related city services demand
reporting_angles: Locate and interview unhoused individuals in Williamsbridge to understand why they're in this district now
Contact NYPD, Outreach Services, and the Mayor's Office of Homelessness to determine if shelter closures or new encampments are driving the spike
Map where the 4 complaints originated to identify hotspot blocks

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Illegal Vending Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints surged to 7 LAST WEEK (367% spike, z-score 4.49) and vendor enforcement complaints spiked 433% TWO WEEKS AGO (z-score 4.6), suggesting coordinated street disorder or organized illegal activity in the district.
evidence: 7 graffiti complaints LAST WEEK vs 1.5 weekly average (367% spike, z-score 4.49)
8 vendor enforcement complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs 1.5 weekly average (433% spike, z-score 4.6)
Parallel timing suggests possible coordinated street presence or gang activity, not isolated incidents
reporting_angles: Request NYPD data on arrests or stops for graffiti or unlicensed vending in the past 2 weeks; interview precinct leadership
Photograph graffiti sites to identify tags, patterns, or territorial markers; consult street art experts on gang symbolism
Interview street vendors and business owners on what enforcement looks like and whether it's effective or creating conflict

themes_detail.label: Food Establishment Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints jumped to 9 LAST WEEK, a 414% spike versus 1.8 weekly average (z-score 3.65), pointing to either a deterioration in food safety compliance across multiple vendors or a sudden increase in inspections.
evidence: 9 food establishment complaints LAST WEEK vs 1.8 weekly average (414% spike, z-score 3.65)
Concurrent with vendor enforcement spike two weeks ago, suggesting possible outbreak or inspection blitz
No constituent services escalations on record, suggesting complaints may not yet have reached elected officials
reporting_angles: Request DOHMH inspection records for Williamsbridge food establishments; identify which establishments have violations and what type (sanitation, temperature, pest activity)
Interview health inspectors on whether a sweep was conducted; ask if a specific violation cluster triggered investigation
Contact a few restaurants/food vendors to understand compliance challenges and costs of remediation

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Enforcement Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints rose to 263 LAST WEEK, a 33% spike from 197.6 weekly average (z-score 5.89), sustained by a broader trend of 2,699 total parking complaints over 90 days, indicating enforcement gaps or resident frustration with limited street space.
evidence: 263 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs 197.6 weekly average (33% spike, z-score 5.89)
2,699 total parking complaints over 90 days (second-highest category after noise), indicating chronic issue
Blocked driveway complaints (1,830 over 90 days) suggest parking spillover is affecting residential access
reporting_angles: Interview parking enforcement officers on whether staffing or patrol schedules changed; request ticket data for recent weeks
Survey residents on whether they've noticed increased illegal parking or enforcement; identify worst blocks
Cross-check with DOT on any recent street changes, permit programs, or zoning that may have altered parking availability
